children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you a few questions to assess your eligibility:

Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Now, do you live with Alex, or if not, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent. Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a couple more questions to make sure I have all the information:

Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or residential accommodation for an extended period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, yes actually - he's been in hospital for a few months now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. It's important to understand the details of this situation as it may affect your eligibility.

How many weeks has Alex been in hospital so far?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in hospital for 15 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (which is more than 12 weeks), this affects your Child Benefit entitlement. However, there are exceptions to this rule.

Do you regularly spend money on Alex while he's in hospital - for example on clothes, toys, treats, or other items for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been able to afford to spend money on his needs while he's in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on your circumstances, you would be **ineligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

Here's why:

Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit since:
- Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- You live with him in the UK
- You're responsible for him
- Nobody else is claiming for him

However, because Alex has been in hospital for 15 weeks (which is more than the 12-week limit), your Child Benefit entitlement has been affected. After 12 weeks in hospital, you can continue to receive Child Benefit only if you regularly spend money on your child while they're in hospital (for example, on clothes, toys, treats, or other items).

Since you've mentioned that you haven't been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's in hospital, this exception doesn't apply to your situation.

**What this means:** Your Child Benefit entitlement would have ended after Alex had been in hospital for 12 weeks.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes home from hospital or if you start regularly spending money on him), you should contact HMRC to discuss your eligibility again.

After the 12-week limit, the claimant is usually no longer entitled to Child Benefit unless an exception applies. The main exception for children in UK hospitals is if the claimant regularly spends money on them. The claimant has stated that they have not been able to afford to spend money on Alex's needs while he's in hospital. Therefore, no exception applies, and the claimant is ineligible for Child Benefit for Alex after the 12-week period has passed.
